floor.says: The same input as a fresh import, loaded plainly into one SQLite file, to read a fresh import against. It is not a lower bound.
floor.total: The same input a fresh import takes in, loaded plainly into SQLite: read and decompress the Bundle, parse it, flatten each resource to one row of a table named for its resource type (a plain value is a column, anything nested is kept as its JSON text) and insert every row into a SQLite file in one transaction, with the SQLite the runtime uses and none of its settings changed. Only the insert is SQL; reading, parsing and flattening are JavaScript. Nested values are kept as JSON text with no further tables, and SQLite's default journal and synchronous settings are kept. It does no mapping to the Cascade vocabulary, keeps no provenance, does no matching of records that are the same, builds no derived views and writes no files, and a faster load of the same input could exist, so it is not a lower bound. The encrypted import is compared with this same unencrypted load. It says what loading costs, not what the import's other work adds up to; the pages do not split the difference beyond the stages the flame graphs measure.

measures.parse: Floor stage: reading the compressed Bundle, decompressing it and parsing the JSON. A fresh import parses the Bundle too: the harness reads, decompresses and parses it once before the import's clock starts, but the import is handed the Bundle's bytes and, from reading its code, parses them again inside its own time (not traced). So this stage and the import's own parsing are about the same work, with this stage also counting reading and decompressing, which the import's clock does not.
measures.flatten: Floor stage: turning each parsed resource into one row of the table for its resource type, plain values as columns and anything nested as its JSON text.
measures.insert: Floor stage: creating a table for each resource type and inserting every row in one transaction into a SQLite file on disk, then closing the file.

counts.rows: How many rows the floor inserted, one for each resource that has a type: a fresh import's count of source entries is every entry of the Bundle.
